finds.quote: **No cross-reference. No announcement.** *One work attempts a procedure and declares it impossible; another retains the machinery and supplies the term that makes it work.*

finds.quote: ⚠ *And Pessoa was reading Plato. Two of the best-documented heteronymists built the Socratic structure, and imitation cannot be distinguished from convergence on the cases available.* **But note what the imitation reading concedes: they imitated it AS a heteronymic architecture** — reading master-disciple-school-death as a way to build authorial positions, and finding it good enough to copy — *a reading of the corpus made by the two moderns best qualified to recognise the operation. Not evidence. Not nothing either.
finds.window: Pessoa's heteronymic architecture; the Socratic master-disciple-school structure
finds.note: Historical thesis about Pessoa (and another heteronymist) building the Socratic structure after reading Plato, and what the imitation reading concedes; the deposit marks it "Not evidence".

finds.quote:
**18.** **This is what keeps Part II from being unfalsifiable by construction.**

**19.** **Stated in advance:** if Plato→Aristotle had fallen **below the heteronymic floor** — outside the constructed-configuration range on the size-matched features — the configurational reading would have been damaged in the ordinary way, and the paper would say so here.

**20.** **It did not happen.** The target sits inside the range. **That is not confirmation and it is not nothing: it is a test that could have gone the other way and went this way.**
finds.points_to: the falsifier "Stated in advance" (Part II §V ¶19): Plato→Aristotle below the heteronymic floor on the size-matched features
finds.note: Records a pre-stated falsifier and that it did not fire; ¶3 (401) calls Part II "the predicted result" while ¶2 says it is carried as reading, not prediction.

finds.quote: **The falsification programme is stated and open:** eight directly-attested contact pairs, each scorable on the same three properties; **one pair producing unannounced, sequence-kept, transformative interlock across an apparatus kills the claim.** Williams→Ginsberg is the sharpest unrun — the master wrote the introduction to *Howl*, announcement by the master being what direct contact characteristically produces.
finds.note: Standing falsifiable claim about what directly-attested contact pairs (schools) produce; falsifier stated in the same sentence; programme unrun.

finds.quote:
## UNRUN, AND NAMED SO THEY CAN BE RUN AGAINST THIS REPORT

**1.** The residual-against-total base rate for the dispersion parity (Part I §2, ¶9a): needs domain classifications for the comparison corpora, which exist only for Aristotle.

**2.** The remainder test (Part I §8, ¶39a): whether anything is invariant across the two corpora's positions that is not explained by shared language, genre or subject — the measure on which the Greek pair would be the same *kind* of object as a documented heteronymic system.
finds.note: List of seven unrun tests (one find per rule 4); quoted by heading and first two items; full list runs to 649.

finds.quote: **[II.4] On the papyrological record.** *Corpus dei Papiri Filosofici Greci e Latini* (Olschki, 1989–) is where independent physical evidence for the corpus's early circulation would be found. **It has not been consulted by this investigation and is named as the standing external check** — the kind of evidence Part II says would bear on the question and this paper does not have.
finds.note: Named standing external check not yet consulted.

finds.quote: No measure below has been calibrated against a model of known collapse state. No threshold, no weight in the composite, and no severity band rests on a measurement — §II.8 says so where the composite is defined, and the calibration it names (produce recursive collapse deliberately on a small model, watch the index evolve, publish that run) has not been done. The reference implementation accompanying this paper is syntax-checked and has never been executed. The reader's test in Part III has been written and not administered.
finds.note: The whole three-grade instrument (gate, self-diagnostic panel, reader's test) specified and never run; calibration run named and not done.

finds.quote: **Two-track reporting, always.** Every Track A score carries the Part II panel on the same checkpoint. The falsifier: Track B inflects before Track A; if Track A proves sensitive first or simultaneously, this Part is weakened.
finds.note: Standing claim that the state-variable track (B) inflects before head-weighted benchmarks (A), with its falsifier.

finds.quote: The prediction worth registering: behavioural contraction (II.1–II.3) and representational contraction (II.6) move together under recursive synthetic training; if they decouple, the instrument has found two phenomena and must say which it is measuring.
finds.note: Tagged prediction about how systems behave (no date/window), so G per rule 3.

finds.quote: It asks the reader who holds two to show, in the passages examined, where the one becomes another — and its wager is that the reader will find, as this paper found, that the passages do not say. That is the paper's result: not that one wrote it, but that two is not established by these passages, which are read as though it were; that the texts offer one as a reading; and that the reading they offer makes better sense of several of them.
finds.window: the passages examined (APr I.31, SE 34, Λ 9, etc.)
finds.note: The paper's stated result as a contestable thesis about the texts: two makers is not established by these passages; framed as a wager on what the reader will find.

finds.quote: In its paragraph, προεξειργασμένον is the class just defined — παρ᾽ ἑτέρων ληφθέντα — and its opposite is ἐξ ὑπαρχῆς. The claim is that this inquiry belongs wholly to the second class: nothing of it was of the received kind.
finds.note: Thesis about what the SE 34 priority claim originally meant (the category is reception), argued from the paragraph.

finds.quote: What this changes in the reading of Λ 9 is small and exact: the celebrated identity is reached by a disjunctive elimination, and the ground given for it is the ground on which such an elimination can select at all.
finds.note: Thesis about the argument-form of Λ 9 and its relation to I.31 (supplies the terminating case).

finds.quote: Why it is more than a recurrent analogy: the figure is kept and the model under it is changed at the exact joint where the *Theaetetus* said its model broke. Not a completion of the wax: the wax re-founded on a different doctrine that keeps the seal.
finds.note: Thesis about textual relation: the De anima/De memoria re-found the abandoned wax model at its exact joint of failure.

finds.quote: what 232a calls unsound is not the accounts but the *appearance* — that there are six things because there are six accounts — and the fault it locates in the beholder is the inference from many accounts to many objects. The passage does not say the accounts are wrong; it says the observer who cannot see what they look toward will count objects by counting accounts.
finds.note: Reading of what the passage originally meant, argued against the observer-error reading.

finds.quote: Or it is a sentence that, while doing all three of those things, distributes to two boys the two marks by which a person is ordinarily recognised — the face to one, the name to the other — and supplies as the criterion of recognising kin something that happens when someone *answers*, so that neither mark is the criterion. The first three are compatible with the fourth. On the fourth, the person is what answers in account: the Greek gives the criterion, διὰ λόγων ἀναγνωρίζειν, and the sentence gives the rest.
finds.note: Fourth reading of the two boys passage, advanced over the standard transition-device reading (n. 8).

finds.quote: What the observation adds is a distinction: the accusation-profile is comic, and the operation — the questioning, the midwifery, the ignorance held as a position — is not in the comic layer at all. Comedy supplied the notoriety; the later corpus occupied the position and differentiated it.
finds.note: Historical thesis on how the Socrates figure was received and occupied.

finds.quote: This section does not solve it. It reclassifies it: under a functional lens, the problem appears as a symptom — the predictable trace of a configuration the biographical model cannot represent — rather than as a question awaiting a biographical answer.

finds.note: Reclassification of the Socratic problem as a symptom of a configuration.

finds.quote: And none of the 144 falls within forty tokens of any of the 46 occurrences of the σιμ- stem — the snub, Aristotle's standing example of form inseparable from matter. Callias takes that slot five times. Where Aristotle needs a face he uses Callias; where he needs a name he uses Socrates.
finds.note: Thesis about what Aristotle was doing with the names Socrates/Callias, from counts in the digitised corpora.
